test_title: SSC MTS Previous Year Paper (Held on: 14 Oct 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A 338-m-long train is travelling at 60 km/h. It crosses a man, travelling in the same direction, in 39 seconds. What is the speed (in m/sec) of the man?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Relative Speed** = Distance ÷ Time = 338 ÷ 39 = 26/3 m/sec.

**Train Speed** in m/sec = 60 × 5/18 = 50/3 m/sec.

In **same direction**, Relative Speed = Speed of Train − Speed of Man.

Speed of Man = 50/3 − 26/3 = 24/3 = 8 m/sec.

**∴ The correct answer is 8 m/sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of the **Train** (L) = 338 m

Speed of the **Train** (Vₜ) = 60 km/h

**Time** taken to cross the man (t) = 39 sec

**Direction:** Same direction

 
 
•

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (Vᵣₑₗ) = Distance ÷ Time

When moving in the **same direction**: Vᵣₑₗ = Vₜ − Vₘ

**Calculations:**

⇒ Convert Train speed to m/sec: Vₜ = 60 × (5/18) m/sec

⇒ Vₜ = 10 × (5/3) = 50/3 m/sec

⇒ Let the speed of the man be Vₘ m/sec.

⇒ Relative Speed = Vₜ − Vₘ = (50/3 − Vₘ) m/sec

⇒ Distance covered = Length of the train = 338 m

⇒ 50/3 − Vₘ = 338 ÷ 39

⇒ 50/3 − Vₘ = 26/3

⇒ Vₘ = 50/3 − 26/3

⇒ Vₘ = (50 − 26) ÷ 3

⇒ Vₘ = 24 ÷ 3 = 8 m/sec

**∴ The correct answer is 8 m/sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concepts

Same Direction: Vᵣₑₗ = V₁ − V₂ | Opposite Direction: Vᵣₑₗ = V₁ + V₂.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Train Crossing Objects

When a train crosses a **stationary point/man**, distance = train length. When crossing a **platform/bridge**, distance = train length + platform length.</p
